text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Tottenham and Chelsea at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
It has been an incredible start to life under Ange Postecoglou for Spurs, with this weekend's results meaning they remain the only Premier League side yet to lose a game this season.

That will be put to the test here in a London derby against a fierce rival, but they know a win will take them back to the Premier League summit and give them a two-point lead over reigning champions Manchester City.

Mauricio Pochettino used to be a hero for Spurs fans, leading their team to the Champions League final in the 2018-19 season, but he returns to his former club here as head coach of rivals Chelsea and could be in for a warm reception from the home crowd.
His new charges are underperforming in the league table, currently 13th, though an upset win here would take them back into the top half.

Postecoglou makes two changes from the 2-1 win at Crystal Palace last time out as Johnson is preferred to Richarlison on the left wing while Udogie returns from injury for Ben Davies, who is missing from the squad altogether with an ankle knock.
Manor Solomon and Ivan Perisic are both long-term absentees with knee injuries, and while Ryan Sessegnon is expected back in November, this game comes too soon for him.

Pochettino goes with four alterations from the 2-0 EFL Cup home victory over Championship side Blackburn Rovers last week, with Silva and Colwill coming into the back four for Badiashile and Cucurella while Caicedo replaces Ugochukwu in midfield.

James starts in the Premier League for the first time since the draw with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the season, while Jackson will lead the line, looking to end a run of three games without a goal.
The two teams enter the pitch in front of a vociferous home crowd at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
The visitors kick us off and we are under way! Can the hosts keep up their unbeaten start? We will find out over the next 90 minutes.
The game has started at a great intensity, with hefty challenges already going in.
Maddison has just been cleared out by Caicedo, and Pochettino will not mind that as his team try to stamp their authority on the match, as long as it does not spill over.
Sarr fires a throughball into the path of Son, but his shot from a difficult angle is saved before a delayed flag goes up for offside.
GOAL!!! KULUSEVKI PUTS SPURS IN FRONT!!! What a start for the hosts as they take the lead after just six minutes! It all comes from Maddison's sweeping pass which sets his team away.
It picks out Sarr, who then lays it to his right for Kulusevski.
The winger cuts onto his left foot before firing goalwards, and he receives a huge slice of luck as the ball deflects off Colwill, wrongfooting Sanchez and flying in.
Postecoglou's men are 1-0 up!
Sarr ran onto Maddison's excellent pass and then played the ball into the path of Kulusevski, who fired home via a deflection.
Spurs smell blood and go searching for a quick second goal, though Sanchez is just about able to hold onto Porro's dipping long-range effort.
This is a huge challenge now for Pochettino's young side.
They are right up against it, and may just need to survive these next 10 minutes before looking for a way back into the contest.
SAVE! Maddison inexplicably gives the ball away under very little pressure, and Sterling puts Jackson in on goal.

The striker hesitates but manages to cut back and find the space to shoot, and his effort looks like it will fly into the bottom corner, until Vicario gets down to his left and palms it behind for a corner.
NO GOAL! Another sweeping move from Spurs carves Chelsea open with a series of perfectly weighted passes.
Bissouma finds Johnson out wide, and he fires in an early cross to pick out Son in the middle.
The forward takes it first time, perhaps catching Sanchez out, and the shot flies past the Chelsea goalkeeper and in.
It is a brilliant attack, but the flag goes up for offside, though there will be a VAR check...
IT REMAINS 1-0! It is very tight, but Son is just about offside and the goal will not count.
That is a shame as it was a lovely move and finish from Spurs and Son.
Spurs are a delight to watch.
Every player is comfortable in possession and they seem to effortlessly slice through their opposition.
Chelsea look a little stunned.
Udogie receives the first booking of the match for a nasty challenge on Sterling.
He seemed to go in with two feet, but while there is a VAR check, the decision is to stay with a yellow card.
He is a lucky boy, and so is Sterling, who could have been in real trouble there if Udogie had fully caught him.
Each of Kulusevski's last two Premier League goals have come at home, after just one of his first eight in the competition had been at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
GOAL!!! STERLING LEVELS FOR CHELSEA!!! They have been under a lot of pressure in these early exchanges, but the persistence of Sterling means they have equalised.
He picks up the ball and carries it into the Spurs box, and receives a big slice of luck as his shot is blocked back into his path.
He brings it down again before finishing, making it 1-1, though there is a VAR review as it seems to hit his arm...
NO GOAL!!! Spurs are very fortunate, as the replays show the ball flicks back up onto Sterling's arm before he finishes, and the goal is ruled out.
Spurs' 1-0 lead remains intact!
Amid all the chaos surrounding the ruled-out Chelsea equaliser, Romero also survived a VAR check that looked to find out whether his petulant kick out at Colwill was worthy of a red card.
He is very fortunate.
GOAL!!! CAICEDO LEVELS WITH A STUNNER!!! A penalty shout falls on defeat ears before the ball finds its way out to Caicedo outside the box.
The former Brighton man smashes goalwards first time, and his shot is superb as it flies past Vicario and into the back of the net.
However, the flag goes up for offside, and there will be a VAR check to ascertain whether Jackson was offside and blocking Vicario's view...
NO GOAL!!! The VAR rules that Jackson was indeed offside and blocking Vicario's view.
However, there is yet another VAR check to see whether a Romero challenge in the build-up to the disallowed goal is worthy of a penalty, and even a red card!
IS THIS A PENALTY AND A RED CARD!?!? The replays show that Romero's challenge on Fernandez in the penalty area is a poor one, catching the Chelsea man high on the leg with his follow-through.
He may have to go here.

ROMERO IS OFF!!! The VAR and on-field referee Michael Oliver decide that Romero's challenge is not only enough to award a penalty, but also see the defender given his marching orders with a straight red card.
It was a poor challenge and could have caused his international team-mate a real problem.
Looking to shore things up after Romero's dismissal, Postecoglou sacrifices Johnson for Dier.
GOAL!!! PALMER MAKES NO MISTAKE!!! The youngster is usually so good from the spot, but he is fortunate this time as Vicario reaches his powerful effort towards the bottom right corner.
The Spurs goalkeeper gets a decent hand to it, tipping the ball onto the post, but it comes off the wrong side of the woodwork for Spurs as it deflects off the frame of the goal and in.
After all of that drama, it is 1-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium!
The ball is in the net again as Sterling squares for Jackson to finish, though the former Manchester City man was offside in the build-up and the flag goes up to curtail the celebrations.
All three of Palmer's goals in the Premier League have been penalties, coming in his last four appearances in the competition.
Spurs have completely lost their heads here, having been in almost complete control at 1-0 up.
Postecoglou now sees yellow for getting too vocal on the touchline.
Maddison is down and looks in serious pain having gone down under no contact.
This is unbelievable for Spurs.

Maddison seems to be okay and looks like he will try to carry on, but with the relief not even having had the time to sink in from that incident, they receive a huge blow as Van de Ven seemingly pulls his hamstring while racing with Jackson after a long ball.
Van de Ven limps off for Hojbjerg.
If that is a torn hamstring, Spurs fans will not be seeing Van de Ven for a fair while, and with Romero now suspended for three games, Postecoglou will have a real problem at centre-back.
They will take no risks with Maddison either, as he makes way for Emerson Royal.
We are into 12 minutes of added time at the end of this first half.
Chelsea are catching this high Spurs line out with throughballs seemingly at will.
The hosts certainly take risks under Postecoglou, but this is just madness with 10 men.

Spurs are yet to lose in the seven previous games in which they have scored the opening goal in the Premier League this season, but that record could be under serious threat if they do not tighten up at the back here.
Chelsea want another penalty as Sterling takes the ball past Porro before going to ground, eliciting a furious response from the Spurs right-back, who believes the winger has dived.
The referee decides not to award a penalty, or a yellow card for simulation.
Jackson goes in the book for cynically bringing down Sarr as Spurs looked to counter.
After that Jackson foul, Colwill and Sarr got into a bit of a scuffle.
The Spurs man sees yellow.
Colwill is also booked for his part in the melee.

Yet another VAR check looks into whether James has elbowed Udogie as the two compete for an aerial ball, and while the Chelsea captain's arm is unnecessarily high, the right-back survives without seeing red.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-1 CHELSEA
The half-time whistle blows to bring a quite unbelievable first half to an end, with both head coaches surely relieved to get their teams back into the changing rooms.

The score is 1-1, with Spurs taking the lead after just six minutes as Kulusevski's shot deflected in, but though the visitors looked like they could get blown away, they responded well and received some much-needed help from the undisciplined hosts.
Romero had already been fortunate not to see red when he petulantly kicked out at Colwill, and he again lost his self-control when he scythed through Fernandez in the Spurs box.
Caicedo's goal seconds after was ruled out for offside, but a VAR review spotted Romero's infringement and awarded a spot-kick before also sending Romero off.

Palmer squeezed his penalty in despite the best efforts of Vicario, and though both sets of players were involved in a scuffle before the interval before James survived a VAR check for a red card, the teams made it into the break at 1-1.

It has been quite the meltdown from Spurs, who seemed to be in complete control at 1-0 up, but a combination of bad luck and ill-discipline mean they may have a job on their hands just to come away with a draw.
After such a frantic first half, surely the pace has to slow a little after the interval, and that will suit the hosts and their 10 men.
Chelsea, on the other hand, will look to stretch the pitch and take advantage late in proceedings.
Colwill was booked in that fracas before half-time, and Pochettino is taking no risks of his own team going down to 10 men as he takes off the 20-year-old at the interval.
Cucurella is on in his place.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Palmer receives the ball just outside the box, gets it out of his feet and pulls the trigger.
His effort is poor in the end, though, and flies well wide.

Five cards were shown in the first half (four yellows, one red), the joint-most in the first half of a Premier League game this season after Aston Villa vs Everton, Burnley vs Chelsea and West Ham vs Chelsea.
Sterling cuts in from the left and shoots from outside the box, though Bissouma's block takes the sting out of the drive and it loops safely into the hands of Vicario.
The first half went on for 56 minutes and 26 seconds, but it was so chaotic that just 23 minutes and 21 seconds of that saw the ball in play.
UDOGIE IS OFF!!! Chelsea break and have a three on two, but Sterling's pass to his right for Palmer is weak and flicked away by Udogie.
The ball is running loose, and as Udogie and Sterling challenge for the ball, the full-back scythes down the Chelsea man, giving the referee no choice but to dig out the second yellow and then a red.
Spurs are down to nine men!
WHAT A MISS! A free-kick routine sees James set away down the right.
The right-back digs a cross out, and Jackson is waiting in the middle only a couple of yards out.
It seems he cannot miss, but his header down into the ground gives Hojbjerg a chance and the substitute manages to hook it over the bar.
Fernandez won the penalty that levelled this game, but now makes way for Mudryk.
His pace could prove a real asset in the latter stages with Spurs' depleted numbers.
Their team are severely outnumbered, but the home fans are responding to their side as they fight to stay in the game.
The pressure is all on Chelsea now to kick on and find a winner in the final half an hour.
James brings down a lofted diagonal ball before lashing goalwards, though his low shot flies wide of the target from a difficult angle.
Kulusevki's goal to put Spurs ahead seems an age ago now with all that has happened since.
He makes way for Skipp as Postecoglou looks to shore things up.
No player had created more chances for Spurs than Sarr's two, but he now trudges off for Bentancur.
Of the 11 Spurs players that started this game, only four now remain on the field, a quite remarkable statistic.
It is all Chelsea now as they look to move the ball and stretch this undermanned Spurs team.
The hosts are so far surviving, though.
UNBELIEVABLE SAVE!!! Spurs continue to live dangerously with this high line, and James lofts a ball over the top for Cucurella.
The substitute is in on goal and cuts back onto his right foot before shooting, but Vicario races out of his goal to close the space and make the stop!
Vicario seemed to take that Cucurella strike square in the face, and though he initially gets up and carries on, he finally goes down to receive some treatment.
Vicario eventually gets back to his feet and the game has resumed.
You suspect the Spurs goalkeeper still has a fair bit of work to do if his team are to keep their unbeaten run alive.
Chelsea are a young side and are looking really naive at the moment.
They just cannot find a way to get past this Spurs defence, despite their numerical advantage.
GOAL!!! JACKSON MAKES IT 2-1!!! Finally Chelsea find a way through as James catches out the high Spurs line with a neat throughball.

Sterling races onto it, takes it into the hosts; box before playing a perfectly weighted squared pass for Jackson, who makes no mistake with the finish as he fires past Vicario to put the visitors ahead!
Sterling's pass across the face of goal was duly finished by Jackson.
Having played some more valuable minutes under his belt after returning from injury, James comes off for Gusto.
NO GOAL! A diagonal free-kick delivery is nodded on by a combination of Bentancur and Silva, reaching Dier at the back post.
The defender catches his first-time volley very sweetly and sends it crashing into the top corner, but the flag goes up for offside and the goal will not count.
There will be a VAR check, though...
IT REMAINS 2-1 TO CHELSEA! The replays show that though it was tighter than it first seemed, Dier is indeed just about offside and the goal remains disallowed, much to the visitors' relief.
All three of Jackson's goals in the Premier League have either been in the 74th minute (one) or 75th minute (two).
Five minutes left at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and the hosts' unbeaten start is in serious peril.
That Dier disallowed goal will have given them hope, though, of finding an unlikely leveller.
Gusto foolishly takes out Emerson Royal, who was going nowhere and was looking for his Chelsea counterpart to foul him.
The Frenchman fell for it, and the hosts will have a free-kick in a great crossing position.
WHAT A CHANCE! After Gusto naively gave the foul away, Bentancur is alert to meet the whipped free-kick delivery from the left.
He is only a couple of yards out, but his header flies wide of the right post.
Mudryk and Vicario come together as both look to race onto a long ball.
The Spurs man got there first, and the Chelsea winger does seem to leave a bit on the goalkeeper, though he only receives a booking.
A subsequent VAR check confirms the challenge was not worthy of a red card.
Sterling has been very lively for Chelsea but is now replaced by Ugochukwu, as we move into nine minutes of additional time.
Spurs are going to give this a go in the final minutes despite their numerical disadvantage.
Chelsea have looked far from comfortable, and Pochettino will be nervous.
CHANCE! Spurs catch Chelsea out and Son races into the visitors' box, making the space for a shot.
His left-footed effort is decent, but Sanchez gets down to his left and saves.
Ugochukwu goes in the book for a foul on Bissouma.
GOAL!!! JACKSON MAKES THE POINTS SAFE!!! After Son had gone close up the other end, Chelsea come forward on the counter and Gallagher receives the ball on the right-hand side.
He slides a pass into the middle for Jackson, and he fires home to make it 3-1 and surely kill the game off!
Gallagher's pass was straight into the path of Jackson, who netted his second of the night with a powerful finish.
GOAL!!! JACKSON SECURES HIS HAT-TRICK!!! Spurs continue to persist with their high line and Chelsea catch them out again.
Jackson takes it deep into the hosts' box, and while he thinks about playing it to his left for Mudryk, he ends up taking it around the goalkeeper and finishing.
It is 4-1!
Palmer played a delightful throughball into the path of Jackson before the striker finished off his hat-trick.
Jackson nearly has a fourth as Mudryk cuts the ball back for him in the penalty area, but he loses his composure and ends up firing high over the crossbar.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-4 CHELSEA
The final whistle goes to bring a quite extraordinary game to an end as Chelsea celebrate a 4-1 victory over nine-man Spurs.
The scoreline does not even begin to tell the story, with the hosts competitive right up until the 94th minute when the Blues finally pulled away.

Spurs took the lead after six minutes as Kulusevki's shot deflected in, but Chelsea responded, thanks in part to Romero's ill-discipline as the defender's high challenge on his international team-mate Fernandez saw him sent off and handed Palmer the opportunity to level from the spot, which he duly did.

The hosts were dealt a further blow when Udogie was shown a second yellow card with 10 minutes of the second half gone, but Chelsea struggled to utilise their numerical advantage against a gutsy Spurs side.
However, the resistance was broken with 15 minutes to play, James sliding Sterling in before he squared for Jackson to finish.

Pochettino's side failed to kill off the game and were nearly pegged back, Dier having a goal disallowed before both Bentancur and Son went close, but the visitors finally put the result to bed in added time, Jackson netting twice to secure his hat-trick and a 4-1 victory.
Spurs' unbeaten start is over, but their fans will be encouraged by a brave display in very tough circumstances.
They remain second, a point off leaders Manchester City, while Chelsea move up to the top half.
Both teams are in Premier League action next weekend, with Postecoglou's men taking on Wolves at Molineux on Saturday before Chelsea host City the following day.
That is all we have from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, so thanks for your time and goodbye!
